definition: The term interlocutory is used to indicate a lack of finality. For example:  An interlocutory decree is a judgment that does not settle all of the issues of a case and where the further action by the court is needed to settle the controversy.  In contrast, a final judgment resolves all issues in dispute and leaves nothing for the court to do but enter judgment.  An interlocutory order is a non-final, temporary order issued during the course of litigation.  An interlocutory appeal is an appeal of a non-final order.
